userStories.title: Missing-image marker carries its position
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Preserve each unreadable transcript image's original position in the schemaVersion 2 load marker.

**Motivation** — The loader writes a bare `[image missing]` per unreadable image (`packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/transcript-images.ts`), so replay cannot tell which image was lost and renumbers the rest.

**Approach** — The loader appends `[image missing #<n>]`, `<n>` the image's 1-based position in the stored message's `images`.

The schemaVersion 2 read appends `[image missing #<n>]` (1-based position in the stored `images`) instead of `[image missing]`.

The load assertions that expect a bare `[image missing]` line now expect `[image missing #<n>]` with the lost image's position; the invariant is unchanged otherwise (one line per lost image, no leading newline on empty content, the readable images kept in order). Enumerate the stored array, not the filtered survivors. Retain existing filesystem safety, error behavior and all-readable behavior. Show regression failures against the old implementation before implementing.

**Scope** — In: schemaVersion 2 image rehydration and existing loader assertions. Out: replay stripping and slot reconstruction (US-004), image labels/titles (US-003), changes to image publication, schema versions or access controls.

**Interface** — The transcript loader (`packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/transcript-images.ts`, the schemaVersion 2 read): appends `[image missing #<n>]`. The seam to US-004 is the content returned by `createFileTranscriptStore.load`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] Loading a schemaVersion 2 transcript whose user message has content `"x"` and two stored images, the second of whose files is missing, returns that message with content `"x\n[image missing #2]"` and `images` holding only the first image.

[unit] Loading a schemaVersion 2 transcript whose user message has content `"x"` and two stored images, both missing, returns content `"x\n[image missing #1]\n[image missing #2]"` and no `images` key.

[unit] Loading a schemaVersion 2 transcript whose user message has empty content and two stored images, the first missing, returns content `"[image missing #1]"` with no leading newline and `images` holding only the second image.

[unit] Loading a schemaVersion 2 transcript whose user message has three stored images, the second missing, returns `images` holding the first and the third in that order and content ending `"\n[image missing #2]"`.
[unit] Loading a schemaVersion 2 transcript whose stored images are all readable returns the content unchanged, with no missing-image line.

routing.reasoning: Small indexed-marker change with existing fixtures; strict isolation applies to the session persistence path and its filesystem safety regression anchors.

userStories.title: Control bytes in the line editor
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Apply terminal backspace bursts as deletions and prevent invisible control bytes entering a draft.

**Motivation** — ink delivers several backspaces arriving in one terminal write as one input string (`"\u007f\u007f\u007f"`, `key.backspace` false); `editLine` inserts it, so the draft holds invisible DEL bytes that are sent to the model.

**Approach** — `editLine` treats an input made only of DEL (`\u007f`) and BS (`\b`) bytes, with no key flag set, as that many backspaces. `insert` first normalises CRLF and a lone CR to a newline (as today), then drops C0 control bytes other than newline and tab, and DEL, from the inserted text.

A DEL/BS run longer than the text before the cursor deletes back to the start of the text; no error. Preserve code-point indexing and existing key/modifier precedence. The mounted ChatInput regression must deliver the burst in one stdin write, not several single-key writes.

**Scope** — In: pure line-editor deletion/insertion behavior and its mounted input seam. Out: focus cursor and owner esc handling (US-008), question dismissal (US-009). DEL or BS bytes mixed with printable text in one input chunk are dropped, not applied as deletions.

**Interface**
```typescript
editLine(state: EditorState, input: EditorKey): EditorResult
```
Target: a DEL/BS-only input deletes that many code points; inserted text loses C0 controls other than `\n` and `\t`, and DEL.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] `editLine` on editor `{ text: "abcd", cursor: 4 }` with input `"\u007f\u007f\u007f"` and no key flag set returns an edit to `{ text: "a", cursor: 1 }`.
[unit] `editLine` on editor `{ text: "abcd", cursor: 2 }` with input `"\b\b\b"` and no key flag set returns an edit to `{ text: "cd", cursor: 0 }`, deleting only back to the start.
[unit] `editLine` on editor `{ text: "abcd", cursor: 4 }` with input `"\u007f\b"` and no key flag set returns an edit to `{ text: "ab", cursor: 2 }`.
[unit] `editLine` on editor `{ text: "", cursor: 0 }` with input `"\u007f\u007f"` returns an edit whose state is `{ text: "", cursor: 0 }`.
[unit] `editLine` on an empty editor with input `"a\u0001b\u007fc"` returns an edit to `{ text: "abc", cursor: 3 }`.
[unit] `editLine` on an empty editor with input `"a\tb\nc"` returns an edit to `{ text: "a\tb\nc", cursor: 5 }`, keeping the tab and the newline.
[unit] `editLine` on an empty editor with input `"a\u001b[0mb"` returns an edit whose text is `"a[0mb"`, the ESC byte dropped.
[unit] `editLine` on an empty editor with input `"\r\n"` still inserts one newline (`{ text: "\n", cursor: 1 }`), as today.
[unit] `editLine` on an empty editor with input `"a\rb"` returns an edit to `{ text: "a\nb", cursor: 3 }`: a lone CR still becomes a newline before control bytes are dropped.
[integration] Rendering `ChatInput` with draft text `"abcd"` and writing `"\u007f\u007f\u007f"` to its stdin in one write publishes a draft whose editor text is `"a"`.

routing.reasoning: Single pure reducer change using existing code-point helpers, with a mounted input regression for Ink chunk delivery.

suggestedCriteria: editLine on `{ text: "a😀b", cursor: 2 }` with a two-byte DEL-only chunk and no key flags returns `{ kind: "edit", state: { text: "b", cursor: 0 } }`, deleting whole code points.

modifiedFiles.reason: `editLine` handles a DEL/BS-only input as repeated backspace, and `insert` strips C0 controls other than newline and tab, and DEL.

userStories.title: Byte-sized image labels and image-free session titles
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Display sub-KiB image sizes accurately and remove image placeholders from titles of sends carrying images.

**Motivation** — `imageSizeLabel` floors every size below 1 KiB to `1 KB`. The session title is the typed text, `[Image #1] what colour...`.

**Approach** — `imageSizeLabel(bytes)` below 1,024 returns `<bytes> B`. `titleWithoutPlaceholders(text)` removes every `[Image #<digits>]`, collapses runs of whitespace to one space and trims; an empty result is `image`; text with no placeholder is returned unchanged. ChatApp passes it as the `title` of a send that carries images.

Update existing label anchors: the `[100, "1 KB"]` image-file case becomes `[100, "100 B"]`, and `imageNoteLabel(1, { data: "AAAA" })` reads `"image 1 · png · 3 B"`. Real PNG/JPEG mention fixtures use their actual byte lengths. The image-entries and chat-app-image-after-send AAAA fixture labels become `image 1 · png · 2×3 · 3 B · clipboard`; remove the comment naming the old 1 KB floor. A hand-written `image · png · 2×3 · 1 KB` mention note may stay as written; row order and kinds are unchanged. Sizes of 1,024 bytes and above retain existing KB/MB labels. Preserve the exact two-argument plain host.send path.

**Scope** — In: image-file labels, pure title helper, ChatApp image-send title wiring and existing label regressions. Out: image slot reconstruction (US-004), leading-placeholder slash parsing (US-005), persistence marker changes (US-001).

**Interface**
```typescript
imageSizeLabel(bytes: number): string
titleWithoutPlaceholders(text: string): string
```
`titleWithoutPlaceholders` is a new export in `image-draft.ts`; a send with images passes `titleWithoutPlaceholders(title)` as its title.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] `imageSizeLabel(178)` returns `"178 B"`, `imageSizeLabel(0)` returns `"0 B"` and `imageSizeLabel(1023)` returns `"1023 B"`.
[unit] `imageSizeLabel(1024)` returns `"1 KB"`, `imageSizeLabel(1536)` returns `"1 KB"` and `imageSizeLabel(350_208)` returns `"342 KB"`.
[unit] `imageSizeLabel(1_572_864)` returns `"1.5 MB"`, as today.
[unit] `imageNoteLabel(1, { mimeType: "image/png", data: "AAAA" })` returns `"image 1 · png · 3 B"`.
[unit] `titleWithoutPlaceholders("[Image #1] what colour is it")` returns `"what colour is it"`.
[unit] `titleWithoutPlaceholders("compare [Image #1]  and   [Image #2] now")` returns `"compare and now"`.
[unit] `titleWithoutPlaceholders("[Image #1][Image #2]")` returns `"image"`.
[unit] `titleWithoutPlaceholders("  two  spaces  ")`, a text with no placeholder, returns `"  two  spaces  "` unchanged.

[integration] In the mounted chat screen with a host whose `acceptsImages()` resolves `true`, attaching a clipboard image through ctrl+v (with `_imageAttachDeps.readClipboard` stubbed to return a PNG) and submitting `"[Image #1] what colour"` calls `host.send` with a third argument whose `title` is `"what colour"` and whose `images` holds that one image.
[integration] In the mounted chat screen, submitting the plain message `"hello"` with no image still calls `host.send("hello", onEvent)` with two arguments.

routing.reasoning: Straightforward pure formatting plus host.send wiring across three source files; requested sessions override applies to session title behavior.

new export `titleWithoutPlaceholders`.
a send with images passes `titleWithoutPlaceholders(title)` as its title.

the `[100, "1 KB"]` case becomes `[100, "100 B"]` and the `imageNoteLabel(1, { data: "AAAA" })` expectation becomes `"image 1 · png · 3 B"`; sizes of 1,024 bytes and above keep their KB and MB labels.
notes of its real PNG and JPEG fixture files read `<n> B`, `<n>` that fixture file's byte length, instead of `1 KB`; every other part of the note is unchanged.

labels of its `data: "AAAA"` fixture images read `3 B` instead of `1 KB` (for example `image 1 · png · 2×3 · 3 B · clipboard`), and the hand-written `image · png · 2×3 · 1 KB` mention note may stay as written; the comment naming the `1 KB` floor goes; row order and kinds are unchanged.
`LABEL` reads `image 1 · png · 2×3 · 3 B · clipboard` (its `data: "AAAA"` fixture) instead of `... 1 KB ...`.

userStories.title: Missing images replay at their numbers
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Reconstruct image slots on resume so missing images retain their numbers without duplicating mention attachment rows.

**Motivation** — The loader writes a bare `[image missing]` per unreadable image (`packages/nax-agent/src/native/session/transcript-images.ts`), so replay cannot tell which image was lost and renumbers the rest.

**Approach** — Replay strips both the numbered form and the old bare `[image missing]` from the trailing run of lines. The message's image slots are its loaded images plus its numbered missing markers, in stored order (the missing positions are re-inserted among the loaded images). The first `slots - mentioned` slots are placeholder images (`mentioned` = the `image`-status records in the message's mention envelope, as `sentEntries` counts today); each gets a row numbered by its slot, `imageNoteLabel(n, image)` for a loaded one and `image <n> · missing` for a missing one. A missing slot inside the mention region gets no row, because the mention's attachment row already names that file. A numbered marker beyond the slot count, and every bare marker, gets today's `image · missing` row after the others. A message whose text is empty once the markers are stripped still gets its slot rows (today's early return for empty text keeps only the bare rows). `sentEntries`' skill branch applies the same rule.

Keep content byte-for-byte when there is no trailing marker run; retain compaction behavior. The loader format is supplied by US-001. The integration test saves genuinely distinct PNGs so deleting the second ref does not also remove a deduplicated first image.

**Scope** — In: history-replay marker parsing, sentEntries optional missing positions, slot rows and backward-compatible bare rows, real file-store-to-replay seam. Out: writing the markers (US-001), size/title labels (US-003), notice classification (US-011). Rewriting transcripts saved by older builds: a bare `[image missing]` keeps its `image · missing` row after the others.

**Interface**
```typescript
sentEntries(message: string, images?: readonly ImageAttachment[], missing?: readonly number[]): readonly TranscriptEntry[]
```
`missing` holds 1-based positions of images lost on load. `replayUser` reads numbered and bare markers and passes the numbered positions to `sentEntries`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] `replayHistory` of a stored user message `{ content: "[Image #1] then [Image #2]\n[image missing #1]", images: [red] }` (red a PNG with source `"clipboard"`) returns the user entry with text `"[Image #1] then [Image #2]"`, then `{ kind: "image", label: "image 1 · missing" }`, then the image entry whose label is `imageNoteLabel(2, red)`.

[unit] `replayHistory` of a stored user message `{ content: "x\n[image missing #2]", images: [a] }` returns the user entry `"x"`, the image entry labelled `imageNoteLabel(1, a)`, then `{ kind: "image", label: "image 2 · missing" }`.

[unit] `replayHistory` of a stored user message `{ content: "x\n[image missing]", images: [a] }` (the bare marker of an older build) returns the user entry `"x"`, the image entry labelled `imageNoteLabel(1, a)`, then `{ kind: "image", label: "image · missing" }`, as today.

[unit] `replayHistory` of a stored user message `{ content: "x\n[image missing #5]", images: [a] }` (a position beyond the message's two image slots) returns the user entry `"x"`, the image entry labelled `imageNoteLabel(1, a)`, then `{ kind: "image", label: "image · missing" }`.
[unit] `replayHistory` of a stored user message whose content is only `"[image missing #1]"` and that has no images returns exactly `[{ kind: "image", label: "image 1 · missing" }]`.

[unit] `replayHistory` of a stored user message `{ content: "[image missing #1]", images: [b] }` returns exactly `{ kind: "image", label: "image 1 · missing" }` then the image entry labelled `imageNoteLabel(2, b)`.

[unit] `sentEntries("look", [a, b], [2])` returns the user entry `"look"`, the image entry labelled `imageNoteLabel(1, a)`, `{ kind: "image", label: "image 2 · missing" }`, then the image entry labelled `imageNoteLabel(3, b)`.
[unit] `sentEntries("look", [a])` with no `missing` argument returns the same entries as today: the user entry, then the image entry labelled `imageNoteLabel(1, a)`.

[unit] `replayHistory` of a stored user message whose content is a mention envelope with one `image`-status record and whose content ends `"\n[image missing #1]"`, with no stored images, returns exactly the envelope's mention entries: the one slot is in the mention region, so no image row is added.

[integration] Saving a schemaVersion 2 transcript through `createFileTranscriptStore` (from `@nathapp/nax-agent`) whose user message `"[Image #1] and [Image #2]"` carries two different PNG images (a 2×3 and a 4×5, so their content-addressed files differ), deleting the file named by the second stored image's `ref` from the transcript's `.images` folder, loading it again and passing the loaded history to `replayHistory` returns the user entry, the image entry labelled `imageNoteLabel(1, first)`, then `{ kind: "image", label: "image 2 · missing" }`.

[unit] `sentEntries` of a skill invocation message with images `[a]` and `missing` `[1]` returns the skill entry, then `{ kind: "image", label: "image 1 · missing" }`, then the image entry labelled `imageNoteLabel(2, a)`.

routing.reasoning: Two existing pure projection modules gain bounded marker parsing and slot reconstruction; the existing public file-store API supplies integration coverage, while the original sessions override still requires strict TDD.

`sentEntries` gains the optional `missing` positions and draws `image <n> · missing` rows in place.

userStories.title: Slash commands after image placeholders
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Execute a slash command following leading image placeholders without spending or losing the pending image draft.

**Motivation** — After `/image a.png` the prompt holds `[Image #1]`, so `/image b.png` typed after it is not a slash line and is sent to the model as text.

**Approach** — `splitLeadingPlaceholders(text)` returns `{ lead, rest }` when `text` is one or more `[Image #<digits>]` placeholders and whitespace followed by a line starting with `/`. ChatApp's `submit` treats `rest` as the slash line: the image refusal checks only images whose placeholder is in `rest`, the prompt is written back to `lead` before the command runs, and the command runs as if `rest` had been typed. The image draft is untouched, so `/image b.png` attaches `[Image #2]` after `[Image #1]`.

Whitespace after a placeholder is optional, as `[Image #1]/image b.png` must split too; preserve the exact lead including whitespace. A leading-placeholder slash line containing a present placeholder in rest runs no command and restores the whole original line via today's `IMAGES_PLAIN_ONLY` refusal. Keep the existing /quit behavior and plain-message send path.

**Scope** — In: pure splitLeadingPlaceholders export and ChatApp.submit/restorePrompt wiring; mounted second-image, model switch, refusal and quit flows. Out: title cleanup (US-003), focus/esc input changes (US-008). Opening the slash menu for a line that starts with image placeholders; the menu opens only for a line that starts with `/`. `/image` with several paths in one command; `/image` keeps taking the rest of the line as one path. A line of image placeholders followed by a slash command, submitted while a turn runs: `ChatInput` keeps today's busy rule (only a line starting with `/` is submitted mid-turn), so it is not run until the turn ends.

**Interface**
```typescript
splitLeadingPlaceholders(text: string): { lead: string; rest: string } | undefined
```
`parseSlashCommand(text): SlashCommand | null` remains null unless its input starts with `/`; ChatApp passes `rest` when split succeeds.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] `splitLeadingPlaceholders("[Image #1] /image b.png")` returns `{ lead: "[Image #1] ", rest: "/image b.png" }`.
[unit] `splitLeadingPlaceholders("[Image #1]/image b.png")` returns `{ lead: "[Image #1]", rest: "/image b.png" }`.
[unit] `splitLeadingPlaceholders(" [Image #1] [Image #2] /model x")` returns `{ lead: " [Image #1] [Image #2] ", rest: "/model x" }`.
[unit] `splitLeadingPlaceholders("/image b.png")` returns `undefined`.
[unit] `splitLeadingPlaceholders("look [Image #1] /image b.png")` returns `undefined`, because text other than placeholders comes before the slash.
[unit] `splitLeadingPlaceholders("[Image #1] hello")` returns `undefined`.

[integration] In the mounted chat screen, after `/image red.png` attaches (the prompt then reads `"[Image #1]"`), typing `/image green.png` after the placeholder and pressing return attaches a second image: the prompt reads `"[Image #1][Image #2]"` and nothing is sent to `host.send`.

[integration] In the mounted chat screen with one attached image, submitting `"[Image #1] /model other-model"` calls the host's model switch with `"other-model"`; typing `describe` and pressing return afterwards calls `host.send` with the message `"[Image #1] describe"` and that one image, because the placeholder and the image draft were kept.

[integration] In the mounted chat screen with one attached image, submitting `"[Image #1] /model x [Image #1]"` runs no command, appends the `IMAGES_PLAIN_ONLY` notice and writes the whole line back to the prompt.
[integration] In the mounted chat screen with one attached image, submitting `"[Image #1] /quit"` closes the chat as `/quit` does.

routing.reasoning: Pure prefix parser and localized command dispatch wiring using existing image draft and imperative prompt handle, with explicit refusal cases.

modifiedFiles.reason: new export `splitLeadingPlaceholders`.
`submit` runs a slash line that follows image placeholders and writes the placeholders back to the prompt first.

userStories.title: The esc layer and its hints
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Introduce one pure top-layer esc model and allow footer/working-line text to describe that layer.

**Motivation** — The footer and the working line say `esc to interrupt` while a card, picker or menu is up, but `ChatApp.tsx` ignores esc whenever one is shown. Esc does close pickers, but nothing says so.

**Approach** — `topEscLayer` reads what is drawn: an ask card (cards render over pickers and the input), then a picker, then the mention picker, then the slash menu, then a running turn. The footer and the working line draw `escHintText(topEscLayer(...))`, and the esc handlers act on the same layer, so the hint and the action cannot disagree. ChatApp passes `turnRunning: turnRunning && keys.canControl()`, `askFromSession: ask.sessionId !== "host"`, `ask` mapped from the pending ask's `type` (`question` → `"question"`, `approval_requested` → `"approval"`, `host_choice` → `"choice"`), `mentionShown: mention.ownsNavigation()` (the mention picker's esc claim, false while only its no-git diagnostic line is drawn) and `menuShown: menuShown()`; a question layer's `stops` is `turnRunning && askFromSession`, which is exactly when the dismiss cancels. The working line's presence is decided as today (from the turn status alone) before the menu rows are measured; only its text takes the esc hint, so the layer can read `menuShown()` without a cycle. The hint texts live in `esc-layer.ts`; `chat-status.ts` (574 lines, under the 600-line gate) only gains the `"layer"` member, `layerHint` and `escHint` parameters, written compactly; if it would pass 600 lines, the hint helpers move into `esc-layer.ts` rather than the gate baseline growing.

Exact hints: question stops=true `esc to close and stop`, otherwise `esc to close`; approval `esc to deny`; choice `esc to cancel`; picker model `esc to close model picker`, resume `esc to close sessions`, mode `esc to close mode picker`, effort `esc to close effort picker`, jobs `esc to close jobs`; mention or slash menu `esc to close menu`; turn/none returns undefined so existing busy/background hints remain. `footerHint` returns `layer` after quit and clear and before busy hints. Existing calls/tests pass layer:false until US-009 wires real screen state.

**Scope** — In: new pure esc-layer module and unit tests, FooterHint layer, layerHint, optional working-line escHint, footerHint precedence. Out: mounted screen integration and AskCard dismissal (US-009), controller decline (US-007), input onEscape (US-008). Changing picker titles; the footer names what esc closes. A mounted-screen test of esc while the keys cannot control the turn (a mode switch in flight); the case is pinned at `topEscLayer` with `turnRunning: false`.

**Interface** — New `EscLayer`, `topEscLayer`, `escHintText` in `src/tui/chat/esc-layer.ts`. Layer results are `{ kind: "question", stops: boolean }`, `{ kind: "approval" }`, `{ kind: "choice" }`, `{ kind: "picker", picker: PickerKind }`, `{ kind: "menu" }`, `{ kind: "turn" }`, `{ kind: "none" }`.
```typescript
workingLine(status, nowMs, glyphs, escHint?: string)
```
`FooterHint` gains `"layer"`; `footerModel({ state, status, hint, copiedChars?, glyphs?, jobs?, tasks?, layerHint?: string })` draws layerHint when hint is layer; `footerHint` input `{ quitArmed, clearArmed, busy, expanded, backgroundable, tmux }` gains `layer: boolean`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] `topEscLayer({ ask: "question", askFromSession: true, picker: "jobs", mentionShown: true, menuShown: true, turnRunning: true })` returns `{ kind: "question", stops: true }`, because a card is drawn over everything else.
[unit] `topEscLayer({ ask: "question", askFromSession: true, mentionShown: false, menuShown: false, turnRunning: false })` returns `{ kind: "question", stops: false }`.

[unit] `topEscLayer({ ask: "question", askFromSession: false, mentionShown: false, menuShown: false, turnRunning: true })` (a host question during a turn) returns `{ kind: "question", stops: false }`.
[unit] `topEscLayer` with `ask: "approval"` returns `{ kind: "approval" }`, and with `ask: "choice"` returns `{ kind: "choice" }`.
[unit] `topEscLayer({ picker: "jobs", mentionShown: true, menuShown: true, turnRunning: true })` returns `{ kind: "picker", picker: "jobs" }`.
[unit] `topEscLayer({ mentionShown: true, menuShown: false, turnRunning: true })` returns `{ kind: "menu" }`, and so does `topEscLayer({ mentionShown: false, menuShown: true, turnRunning: false })`.
[unit] `topEscLayer({ mentionShown: false, menuShown: false, turnRunning: true })` returns `{ kind: "turn" }`, and with `turnRunning: false` returns `{ kind: "none" }`.
[unit] `escHintText({ kind: "question", stops: true })` returns `"esc to close and stop"` and `escHintText({ kind: "question", stops: false })` returns `"esc to close"`.
[unit] `escHintText({ kind: "approval" })` returns `"esc to deny"` and `escHintText({ kind: "choice" })` returns `"esc to cancel"`.

[unit] `escHintText` for picker `"model"`, `"resume"`, `"mode"`, `"effort"` and `"jobs"` returns `"esc to close model picker"`, `"esc to close sessions"`, `"esc to close mode picker"`, `"esc to close effort picker"` and `"esc to close jobs"`.
[unit] `escHintText({ kind: "menu" })` returns `"esc to close menu"`; for `{ kind: "turn" }` and `{ kind: "none" }` it returns `undefined`.
[unit] `footerHint({ quitArmed: false, clearArmed: false, busy: true, expanded: false, backgroundable: true, tmux: false, layer: true })` returns `"layer"`.
[unit] `footerHint` with `quitArmed: true` and `layer: true` returns `"quit"`, and with `clearArmed: true` and `layer: true` returns `"clear"`.

[unit] Given the existing host state and turn status fixtures, `footerModel` with `hint: "layer"` and `layerHint: "esc to close jobs"` returns a left line whose hint text is `"esc to close jobs"` after the mode label.
[unit] `workingLine(runningStatus, nowMs, glyphs, "esc to close and stop")` returns a line whose muted detail ends `"esc to close and stop)"`, the escape hint taking the place of `esc to interrupt`.
[unit] `workingLine(runningStatus, nowMs, glyphs)` with no `escHint` returns the same detail as today, ending `"esc to interrupt)"`.

routing.reasoning: Pure layer selection and hint composition across existing UI helpers; no permission decisions or session side effects are introduced here.

modifiedFiles.reason: `FooterHint` gains `"layer"`, `footerModel` takes `layerHint`, and `workingLine` takes an optional `escHint`.
`footerHint` takes `layer` and returns `"layer"` after quit and clear and before the busy hints.
`footerHint` calls that build the input object gain `layer: false`, with the same expected hints; no expected text changes.

userStories.title: Declining a question
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add an explicit question decline operation that settles host and session questions without answering an approval.

**Motivation** — A question card shows no choices and its answer box looks exactly like the chat input; esc does nothing on it (`AskCard.tsx` returns early from `useInput` for a question).

**Approach** — `ChatAskController.declineQuestion(requestId)` settles a host question with `null` (what its timeout does today) and answers a session question with the text `QUESTION_DECLINED_REPLY` (`"The user closed the question without answering."`), then removes it from `pending()`.

`declineQuestion` with an id that is not an open question has no effect, no answer sent. Reuse host-question cleanup to clear the timeout and abort listener; remove once so onChange fires once. Add the method to both interface and class, and export the constant through `@/chat`. Update only hand-built controller stubs in test/ui/chat/ask-card.test.tsx, chat-app.test.tsx, chat-app-mentions.test.tsx and slash-commands.test.tsx with `declineQuestion: () => {}`; their existing assertions do not change.

**Scope** — In: controller method, constant/barrel export, settlement and no-op tests, interface-consumer fixture compatibility. Out: ChatInput routing (US-008), card/screen dismissal and host.cancel (US-009), layer hints (US-006). Changing what esc does on approval cards (deny) and choice cards (fallback choice); neither stops the turn.

**Goal** — Wire the drawn top esc layer into chat hints and key actions, including declining and conditionally stopping a session question.

**Motivation** — The footer and the working line say `esc to interrupt` while a card, picker or menu is up, but `ChatApp.tsx` ignores esc whenever one is shown. Esc does close pickers, but nothing says so.

**Approach** — `topEscLayer` reads what is drawn: an ask card (cards render over pickers and the input), then a picker, then the mention picker, then the slash menu, then a running turn. The footer and the working line draw `escHintText(topEscLayer(...))`, and the esc handlers act on the same layer, so the hint and the action cannot disagree. ChatApp passes `turnRunning: turnRunning && keys.canControl()`, `askFromSession: ask.sessionId !== "host"`, `ask` mapped from the pending ask's `type` (`question` → `"question"`, `approval_requested` → `"approval"`, `host_choice` → `"choice"`), `mentionShown: mention.ownsNavigation()` (the mention picker's esc claim, false while only its no-git diagnostic line is drawn) and `menuShown: menuShown()`; a question layer's `stops` is `turnRunning && askFromSession`, which is exactly when the dismiss cancels. The working line's presence is decided as today (from the turn status alone) before the menu rows are measured; only its text takes the esc hint, so the layer can read `menuShown()` without a cycle.

Question card: decline the question; then, for a question the chat session asked (not a host question from a run ask or a job, whose `sessionId` is `"host"`), `host.cancel()` when a turn runs and `keys.canControl()` (AskCard via `onDismiss`, ChatApp). The question card's input placeholder is `type your answer · enter to send`. A running but uncontrollable turn is passed as turnRunning:false to the helper and only closes the question; its excluded mounted mode-switch test is represented by US-006's false case.

Use the same layer for the screen's turn-escape guard and hints, allowing only the layer's owner to act. Preserve existing picker/menu closes, approval deny, choice fallback, idle double-esc clear, and copied/quit/clear hint precedence. Map host_choice safely because it has no sessionId. Keep ChatApp changes to wiring, and keep chat-status under 600 lines without raising a baseline.

userStories.title: Background notice summaries
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Parse canonical background notice text into stable one-line presentation summaries.

**Motivation** — Background notices fill the transcript: `useJobs` delivers each notice through `sendTurn({ message })` (`ChatApp.tsx`, the `deliver` option), so `sentEntries` lays it out as a highlighted `user` entry; replay does the same.

**Approach** — A task line is matched from `[nax-tasks] background command <id> (` to the first `) ended: <state>,` after it, and a job line from `[nax-jobs] job <id> (<kind> <target>) ended: <state>`, `<state>` being the single word after `ended: `. `summarizeBackgroundNotice(text)` (`packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/notice-summary.ts`, beside the builders that write the notices) returns a one-line summary for a notice and `undefined` for any other text.

Task summaries count matched commands and states in first-seen state order, using singular `1 background command ended` and plural `3 background commands ended`, then ` · <count> <state>` per state. Job summaries read `nax job <kind> <target> ended · <state>`, ignoring cost, note, log and chain lines. A `buildRunAskNotice` first line `[nax-jobs] run ask <askId>` yields `run ask <askId> sent to the agent`. A notice-looking text that matches no known notice line returns undefined. Test with outputs of the canonical builders rather than changing those builders to suit the parser. Export through `@/prompts`.

**Scope** — In: pure summary parser next to notice builders and its barrel export. Out: transcript kind/projection/layout/click behavior (US-011), output listings (US-012). Changing the text the model receives in a background notice. Task commands containing a newline or the text `) ended:`: such a notice may summarise wrongly or fall back to the user row.

**Interface**
```typescript
summarizeBackgroundNotice(text: string): string | undefined
```
